name: manual_22715d
claim: Never copy a scanner baseline regenerated by another pull request to make a security scan pass. Reproduce the scan locally with the pipeline flags, count new findings on the base tree and on your branch, read each finding in the files you changed, fix the avoidable ones in code, and check the real exit code: a CI mode that fails only on high severity may need no baseline change at all. Send any baseline refresh as its own reviewed change.

decisions.notes: A baseline of about 150 opaque hashes was cherry-picked into a stacked branch and its commit message called the findings expected without anyone reading them. Running the scan locally showed the base tree already had 170 new findings, the branch added six, four of them real high findings (a hook writing its log inside the Claude configuration directory), and that with those four fixed the scan exits 0 on the old baseline, so the baseline change was unnecessary.
